Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps

Hi Simon / Emma —

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation and helpful context on the customer support use case and throughput targets. Below is a concise post-demo recap and an initial model shortlist with rationale (cost / latency / quality tradeoffs). I’ve attached a 1‑page PDF and the prompt set we used for the demo.

Recap / goals:
- Goal: extract structured entities and generate concise multi-sentence summaries for support tickets (avg length ~200 tokens).
- SLA targets you mentioned: p50 latency <= 200ms for single-turn completions (512 tokens), predictable cost at scale, and strong factuality on ticket summaries.
- Success metric for POC: quality >= 85% on your evaluation prompt set + p50 latency within ~2x of target under typical traffic.

Initial recommended shortlist (qualitative):
1) Mistral-Instruct-7B (FP16) — Best balance of latency and cost. Strong instruction-following and low per-token cost; good for real-time single-turn summarization.
   - Cost: low 
   - Latency: low (p50 expected <150ms on a single A10G-like instance for 512 tokens)
   - Quality: good for instruction tasks; may struggle on heavy domain-specific factuality without prompt tuning

2) Llama-2-13B (4-bit quant) — Higher quality, higher resource needs.
   - Cost: medium
   - Latency: medium (p50 ~250–400ms depending on quantization and instance)
   - Quality: better long-form reasoning and factuality; recommended if you prioritize accuracy over raw latency

3) Falcon-40B (quantized, batch-optimized) — Highest quality for complex content, but much higher cost/latency. Consider for cases where accuracy is critical and you can tolerate higher latency or use it as a fallback tier.
   - Cost: high
   - Latency: high
   - Quality: best of the three on nuanced reasoning/factuality

Suggested POC approach:
- Phase 1: Run parallel evals on your prompt set (attached: acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl) across #1 and #2, measure quality, p50/p95 latency, and cost per 1M tokens.
- Phase 2: If #2 shows meaningful quality wins, test hybrid routing (default to #1; fallback to #2 for low-confidence cases).

Deliverables attached / links:
- acme_post_demo_model_shortlist.pdf (attached) — one-page summary and recommendation matrix
- acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (attached) — the prompts we ran during the demo
- Evaluation report (internal link): https://redwood-inference-benchmarks.internal/acme/2026-10-28/report.html
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345678

Next steps / asks:
- Can you share a representative sample of 200–500 real tickets for a short POC (anonymized)?
- Do you want us to run the initial evals on your dataset or should we use the attached prompt set first?
- If yes to POC, what’s your availability next week for a 30–45m kickoff with engineering?

I’ll loop Rafael (SE) and Priyom (Solutions) on logistics and a proposed evaluation script.

Thanks —

Thanks Simon — quick answers and proposed plan below. (See Rafael’s technical note after this email for infra/eval specifics.)

Latency / cost quick answers:
- Mistral-Instruct-7B: should hit p50 < 200ms for 512-token completions on a single A10G-like instance with our serving runtime and caching; typical cost estimate: ~$150–$300 per 1M tokens (depends on batching and deployment).
- Llama-2-13B (4-bit): p50 typically ~250–350ms for comparable single-instance configs; cost estimate: ~$400–$700 per 1M tokens (quantized, depends on kernels).

POC plan and ask:
1) Please upload the anonymized 300-ticket sample to the Drive folder linked here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-model-evals (or share via secure link).
2) We’ll run parallel evals across Mistral-7B (FP16) and Llama-2-13B (q4) using your sample + attached acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl.
3) Deliverables within 5 business days of receiving data: per-prompt quality metrics, p50/p95 latency, and an estimated cost model for steady-state.

Eval script (what we’ll run):
- 3 cold runs followed by 3 steady-state runs
- p50/p95 latency for 512-token completion, throughput at target concurrency (you’ll confirm concurrency in kickoff)
- A/B quality measurement: exact-match entities + human-rated summary quality (1–5) on a 200-sample subset

Kickoff: I’m available Thu 10/29 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 10/30 09:00–10:00 PT. Which works for Emma / your eng team?

Quick SE note on infra and eval knobs (adding here for visibility):

- Quantization: For Llama-2-13B, q4_0 / q4_k moments work best with our kernel selection for throughput; expect ~20–30% memory savings but slightly higher p50 vs more aggressive q5 variants.
- Batching: Keep single-request latency tight by using small max_batch_size (2–4) for the user-facing route, and larger batches for offline bulk processing.
- KV cache: not relevant for single-turn summaries, but useful if you later add multi-turn context.
- Recommended instance choices (starting point):
   - Mistral-7B: 1 x A10G-equivalent for low-latency serving
   - Llama-2-13B (q4): 1–2 x H100/80GB-equivalent (or multi-GPU with model sharding) for predictable p95 under concurrency
- Monitoring hooks: add token-level latency and model confidence thresholds to automatically route high-uncertainty inputs to the higher-quality model (Llama-2-13B) as a fallback

I’ll prepare a short config yaml to attach to the kickoff doc (perf hints and quant settings).
